scope: Frame-by-frame SE comparison of rendered 3D pose guide and current painted trial. This records visible pose correspondence; it does not claim automatic hand/grip detection or validate unseen anatomy.

applied_checks: compare visible grip-to-tip direction at each frame
check weapon continuity and visible hand attachment
reject the effect if it disguises a body or weapon-pose mismatch
research_method.automated_pose_audit: not run: no hand-annotated tip/grip points are bound to this generated sheet; review is visual and therefore does not claim numeric alignment scores

frame_review.painted: frame 0 has a longer down-right blade; frame 1 opens the arm while the blade remains low
frame_review.result: weak match; sword angle and arm timing diverge

frame_review.guide: the guide transitions into its raised sword pose by frame 3
frame_review.painted: frame 2 is already overhead and frame 3 remains overhead
frame_review.result: transition starts early and loses the guide intermediate pose

frame_review.guide: low forward extension; the blade remains pointed forward across several samples
frame_review.painted: horizontal forward blade is held across the same interval with little blade-angle change
frame_review.result: direction is partly similar, but the repeated hold reads as a thrust and not a lateral cut

frame_review.guide: blade rotates toward recovery near the body
frame_review.painted: blade sweeps up and back through noticeably different angles
frame_review.result: weapon path does not track the guide; transition looks abrupt

frame_review.painted: several recovery blades switch between down, hidden, and guard angles
frame_review.result: silhouette / blade continuity is not consistent enough for a master

findings: The sword in the painted 4x4 trial does not match the guide reliably frame by frame.
The 3D source guide itself reads as a forward thrust: frames 4-8 hold a long forward extension without a distinct cross-body cut.
Trail timing cannot repair the gesture. Do not treat iteration 6 or the iteration 8 WeaponLight composite as production art.
Replace the attack motion and render a new guide before painting the high-detail 8x16 BasicAttack master and cutouts.
